newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says no action as baht slides versus dlr.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says no action as baht slides versus dlr.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said on Thursday that there was no need to take action to shore up the baht which has fallen to a 56-month low against the recently strong U.S. dollar.

"There is no need to take any action. Against other majors, the value of the baht has remained constant on a weighted average basis. It is only against the dollar that it has dropped," a Bank of Thailand official told Reuters.
Another central bank official confirmed that the baht's mid-rate against the U.S. dollar, which is fixed daily by the central bank, had fallen to it lowest level since May 1992.
Thursday's mid-rate was fixed at 25.67 and the baht was trading at around 25.655/659 against the dollar at 0710 GMT.
The baht's midrate is calculated by the central bank daily against a basket of currencies dominated by the U.S. dollar. The central bank keeps the basket confidential.
Dealers said the baht's position against the U.S. dollar now depended on how the currently strong American unit moved against other majors in the coming weeks.
